transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Korva Coleman.
The midterm elections are tomorrow.
The University of Florida election lab says more than 54 million Americans have cast early
ballots.
NPR's Tamara Keith says many voters are unhappy.
The average price of a regular gallon of gas is over $4 a gallon.
Inflation is up.
They're worried about artificial intelligence and data centers.
The war with Iran is unpopular and looming over everything, and voters are increasingly
voicing concerns about corruption.
NPR's Tamara Keith reporting.
Michigan Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens has revoked her endorsement of Democratic
Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.
Instead, she is endorsing Republican Mike Rogers.
Stevens lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed.
She says he has not done enough to distance himself from an outside ad critical of Israel.
The Alaska Senate race has been rocked by a New York Times report.
There are allegations aides working for Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola helped recruit
a third Senate candidate to try to spoil the campaign of Republican incumbent Senator Dan
Sullivan.
Peltola has strongly denied involvement, and PR has not independently verified the allegations.
Alaska public media's Liz Ruskin has more.
Several voters said they'd had it with negative ads and ignored the Times story.
Rose Ellis credits Peltola for holding up under pressure.
I say kudos, and again, you know, a strong, independent, indigenous woman.
Twenty-two-year-old voter Griffin Lindsay thinks the allegations have hurt the Democrat.
He went door-to-door for Peltola.
I've heard people are getting worked up about it, and I think that it has made an impact,
yes.
A Judge Sunday dismissed a federal lawsuit aiming to block election certification if
the Senator narrowly loses.
The Justice Department says it will appeal.
For NPR News, I'm Liz Ruskin in Anchorage.
Lindsay Clancy will be back in a Massachusetts courtroom today for a hearing that could determine
if she will face another trial for the deaths of her children.
From Member Station WBUR, Deborah Becker has more.
Prosecutors say although the first case ended in a mistrial, they should be allowed to continue
to "pursue justice" for the three Clancy children.
Criminal defense attorney Keith Halpern, who is not involved in the case, expects another
trial.
I don't think there was ever any question that they were going to retry this case in
one form or another.
The defense argues the mistrial was a mistake, and the judge should have further investigated
claims that one juror wouldn't follow the law.
The defense is not disputed that Clancy killed her children, but said she was experiencing
severe psychosis.
For NPR News, I'm Deborah Becker in Boston.
You're listening to NPR.
There appears to be another cyberattack underway against refrigerators and freezers in some
European countries.
Dozens of grocery stores in Belgium, Sweden, and Luxembourg say the temperatures in some
of their freezers are spiking to more than 120 degrees.
There was a similar cyberattack last month in France.
In the U.S., there are new flash flood warnings posted for the Four Corners area.
Heavy rain in Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, and Utah has flooded rivers and forced some
evacuations.
The album by My Chemical Romance, called The Black Parade, has now reached the top of the
Billboard Album charts, but that's happening 20 years after the album was originally released.
That means the album now holds the record for the longest amount of time between release
date and the top of the charts.
Andrew Limbong has more.
If you're of a certain age and you've ever stepped foot in a hot topic, here's something
that'll perk your ears.
My Chem's The Black Parade, a concept album about death and grief, came out in 2006 and
was a high watermark for the band.
The band is now currently on a huge worldwide tour, celebrating the album complete with
a new 20th anniversary reissue on vinyl, CD cassette.
According to Billboard, the album's jump to number one was driven mostly by pure album
sales as opposed to streaming.
Andrew Limbong, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR.
Want to hear this podcast without sponsor breaks?
Amazon Prime members can listen to NPR News now, sponsor free through Amazon Music.
Or you can also support NPR's vital journalism and get NPR+ at plus.npr.org.
That's plus.npr.org.

topics.text: Midterm elections tomorrow; over 54 million Americans have cast early ballots, per University of Florida lab
Voters express unhappiness over gas prices above $4 a gallon, inflation, AI, data centers, and Iran war
Michigan Rep. Haley Stevens revokes endorsement of Abdul El-Sayed, endorses Republican Mike Rogers
Alaska Senate race rocked by New York Times report alleging Mary Peltola aides recruited spoiler candidate
Judge dismisses federal lawsuit seeking to block Alaska election certification; Justice Department to appeal
Lindsay Clancy hearing in Massachusetts could determine whether she faces retrial for children's deaths
Cyberattack apparently targets refrigerators and freezers at grocery stores in Belgium, Sweden, and Luxembourg
Flash flood warnings issued for Four Corners area after heavy rain in Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, Utah
My Chemical Romance's The Black Parade reaches Billboard album chart number one, 20 years after release
